subject.title: [Bug]: Discord sessions persist per-session exec directives, causing allowlist mode to behave unexpectedly after config changes

question: Should persisted per-session `/exec` fields be allowed to override later stricter global or agent exec security config after Discord sessions resume?
rationale: Current source, tests, and docs intentionally preserve per-session `/exec` defaults, but the reported failure mode is security-sensitive because old session state can shadow later operator policy changes.

options.title: Clamp to operator policy
options.body: Treat global or agent exec security config as the maximum allowed policy and clear or clamp stored session fields that exceed it, with focused upgrade/reset coverage.

options.title: Keep session persistence
options.body: Document that operators must reset sessions or use a repair flow to enforce changed exec policy for existing Discord lanes.

options.title: Ship reset first
options.body: Add an operator-facing session exec reset or doctor repair before changing precedence semantics for existing sessions.

recommendation.title: Clamp to operator policy
recommendation.body: Treat global or agent exec security config as the maximum allowed policy and clear or clamp stored session fields that exceed it, with focused upgrade/reset coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: The clearest feature-history trail for `/exec` session overrides and focused tests points to steipete.
